outcomes: A route tree declared by files renders the same nested page, layout, error, loader, and action graph on the server and in the browser
An application chooses SSR, static generation, revalidation, or bounded islands explicitly and can review the resulting client-JavaScript budget
Loaders read and actions mutate server-side state through validated input and request-scoped dependency injection
Server authorization, CSRF, CSP, cache isolation, and hostile hydration-data handling stay effective when client JavaScript is absent, delayed, or broken
nonGoals: React Server Components, a general browser bundler, or inferring a rendering mode from component source
Treating client-side route visibility as authorization or serializing tokens and personally identifiable claims into the browser
Owning OAuth identity establishment, API streaming, UI styling, or persistence implementations supplied by other framework packages
Promising compatibility across every pre-1.0 minor release

text: Publication builds the default SSR entry and browser entry as separate graphs;
the browser graph exports client helpers but contains no SSR implementation or server-only runtime import.

Generation maps page, layout, loader, action, error, not-found, dynamic segment, route group, and prefixed scan-root files into one deterministic nested route graph with matching server and client route identifiers;

a layout declares no action, so a submission to a layout's own address, with or without the `index` query parameter, reaches the action of its index page, whichever of the two files registers first, and a layout whose index page has no action answers 405.

requirements.text: After a client navigation, the hydrated app scrolls a new location to the top or to its hash target, keeps the browser's scroll to the target of a link to an in-page `#id`, restores the saved position on back and forward, keeps the position when the navigation asks to, and leaves the server markup unchanged.

text: A back or forward step that changes or drops only the fragment keeps the loaded data and runs no loader, unless a route's `shouldRevalidate` returns true;
a submission or a `revalidate()` call still runs the loaders.

requirements.text: A loader or action redirect, whether the server signals it or fetch already followed it, stays in the router when the router renders its target, and loads the target as a new document when it is a same-origin path the router does not render, such as a server-only page, a path outside the basename, or a path only a not-found catch-all matches.

A Link that changes only the query or the hash navigates, a Link to the current URL replaces the entry and re-runs the route loaders, a `#` or empty target is a placeholder that runs its own click handler without navigating, intent prefetch loads the target route, and outside a router a Link renders a plain anchor with the same props.

text: On client navigation, a layout loader fetches the JSON endpoint the server registers at the layout's path: each dynamic segment is filled from the matched params and URL-encoded, a trailing catch-all is dropped, and the mounted basename and the request query string are kept;
a missing required param fails the loader without a request, and the server answers that endpoint with the same loader and params as the server render.
Generation resolves shared and React settings independently, gives nested project react settings precedence over package metadata, and retains flat package.json#putnami compatibility.

A known React-only key placed directly at options["@putnami/web:generate"].<key> fails before route scanning or artifact writes and names options["@putnami/web:generate"].react.<key> as the corrected path.

requirements.text: SSR runs the static handler and loaders before rendering, keeps redirects, router status and a loader `HttpException`'s own status, on a client navigation too, logs an unexpected loader error and records it as the request error, then emits one HTML document whose React body streams and whose timer is released on success or error. Loaders and render stop when their request ends, logging and recording no error. Loaders run under an `ssr loaders` span and the shell under an `ssr render` span.

A browser request receives the head and the React shell once the shell is ready, and each Suspense boundary streams as it resolves. The head holds the contributions known at the shell; an extracted Emotion style a later chunk needs is written before that chunk; other late styles, scripts, and title, meta and link tags are written after the root, the tags by one nonced script. A request whose user agent matches the crawler pattern, and a page whose HTML is cached, wait for every boundary.

Title, language, meta, link, style, and script contributions are held in per-request context during SSR and de-duplicated in the browser, so interleaved requests cannot read or clear one another's document state.

text: Hydration serializes loader, action, error, basename, timeout, and bounded role/scope state with script-safe escaping;
a chunk or hydration failure preserves or restores server HTML instead of blanking the page;
the server and the generated client routes build the same element for a page, so a server-rendered page hydrates in place without a recoverable error.
Only page().static() selects SSG or ISR;
static loaders execute in a request-free context, request access raises StaticRenderViolation, dynamic paths cannot escape the output root, and routes without finite paths remain live.

requirements.text: When a pre-rendered page shows a build version that ends with its commit suffix, static prerender records that version beside the static HTML, and serving the SSG or ISR page at its route replaces it with the running build's version, so a page restored from the build cache or deployed under another release id shows the running version.

A static page ships no full-page hydration bundle, serializes script-safe island props into named boundaries, and hydrates each island only by its declared load, idle, visible, or media strategy with a safe immediate fallback when the requested browser observer is unavailable.

text: Loader and action builders validate and coerce declared input, resolve declared dependencies from the active request scope, and execute their handlers only on the server;
an action that returns nothing answers 204 No Content, on the HTTP route as in the router;
browser builder middleware methods cannot import or execute server middleware.
Security middleware declared on a layout or page wraps its SSR page, loader JSON endpoint, action endpoint, and not-found boundary, including lazy descendants;
routes outside that layout remain unaffected.

requirements.text: Hydration serializes only authentication, role, and scope facts for UI gating, treats function guards as indeterminate and denied on the client, and never treats that hint as a replacement for server middleware.

text: React routes apply CSP with a per-request nonce, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and action CSRF validation by default;
state-changing submissions require the cookie token echoed by the client header or no-JavaScript form field unless the application explicitly opts out.

requirements.text: Default page-cache keys include a stable user fingerprint and query string, loader-cache keys include query parameters, redirects are not cached, and successful actions evict every declared static or computed pattern.

Every build serializes a sorted, newline-terminated route manifest containing mode, hydration, DI proof, and per-route client-JavaScript bytes, and the budget gate rejects absolute or baseline-relative regressions deterministically.

A page module may export proves, a list of {feature, requirement, at}; the build writes each entry into the page routes of the route inventory whose path admits at, and a malformed list, or an at that no route of the page admits, fails the build.
